newsitem.title: USA: Unisys posts eight-fold profit improvement.
newsitem.headline: Unisys posts eight-fold profit improvement.

text.p: Unisys Corp. said Monday that greater cash flow and improved operating margins helped it increase profits eight-fold in the second quarter.

The computer maker said its net income for the three months ended June 30 soared to $41.9 million from $5.3 million in the year-ago period. After a payment of $27.8 million in preferred dividends, its profit equalled 8 cents a share, which compared with a loss of 14 cents a share a year ago.
Unisys' earnings were better than most Wall Street expectations. According to First Call, which tracks analysts' estimates, the consensus estimate was for a profit of 5 cents a share.
Unisys' stock gained 62.5 cents to $8.81 on the New York Stock Exchange, where it was one of the most heavily traded issues.
Revenue for the quarter rose 5 percent to $1.59 billion from $1.51 billion, despite the negative impact of currency translations in international markets.
The company said it posted double-digit revenue growth in the United States and revenue from international markets improved slightly from a year ago.

"We continued to build momentum in the quarter," Chairman James Unruh said in a statement. "Revenue was up, cash flow improved, and our operating profit margin almost doubled from a year ago to a margin rate of 8.1 percent of revenue."
The company, which is based in Blue Bell, Pa., said it saw solid performance in both its services and technology sectors.
Its Computer Systems Group turned in another very good profit and revenue performance and its Information Services Group continued to make progress toward profitability.

"The efforts we have been making to transform our business portfolio and move into higher-growth markets are clearly paying off," Unruh said. "Operating expenses as a percent of revenue continue to decline. We are on track to achieve our financial goals for the year."

Unisys said revenue from its Computer Systems Group grew 10 percent on continued strong demand for its ClearPath enterprise servers, which allow clients to run proprietary Unisys systems and industry-standard systems such as Windows NT and UNIX on the same platform.
The group's gross profit margin was up 5 percentage points from year-ago levels.
Unisys also said the Information Services Group was on target to achieve operating profitability by the end of the year and to return to a sustainable revenue growth rate.
The group improved its gross profit margin by 3 percentage points to 21.3 percent while narrowing its operating loss to $17.8 million from $49.5 million in the first quarter.

However, revenue was down 5 percent, reflecting continued focus and refinement of the group's business model. Orders posted a strong double-digit year-over-year gain for the second consecutive quarter.
Unisys said its Global Customer Services group revenue increased 11 percent, driven by continued strong growth in the strategic area of distributed computing support services.
The company said its overall orders in the quarter were up slightly from year-ago levels, which included a large order from the U.S. Social Security Administration.
Unisys also said that its cash flow performance continued to improve during the quarter.

The company also announced it reached an agreement with a syndicate of banks for a new two-year, $200 million revolving line of credit, replacing a one-year, $200 million revolving credit facility that expired in June.
For the first six months, Unisys said it posted net income of $61.2 million, or 2 cents a share, compared with a loss of $8.1 million, or 40 cents a share, after preferred dividends.
Revenue expanded to $3.12 billion from $2.93 billion.

Separately, Compaq Computer Corp. said Monday it has designated Unisys' Global Customer Services as a regional service provider. Unisys can deliver Compaq service offerings via contract for North American customers running mission-critical, distributed computing applications.
Since 1996, Unisys has been providing services to Compaq customers in Latin America, the Caribbean and Japan. Terms were not disclosed.
